newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian oil center hit by wildcat strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian oil center hit by wildcat strike.

text.p: The oil production centre of Barrancabermeja in northern Colombia was hit by a wildcat strike on Friday called to protest against the killing of a top labour union official.

Cesar Carrillo, a leader of the 6,000-strong state oil workers union known as USO, said the strike began at midnight on Thursday (0500 GMT Friday) and that it had paralysed most refinery and oil pumping operations in the industrial city on the banks of Colombia's Magdalena river.
Speaking in a telephone interview, he said the strike would last "indefinitely" and that it was called to protest against the killing of USO vice president Rafael Gonzalez.
Gonzalez, who owned a restaurant in Barrancabermeja, was shot dead by a lone gunmen who entered the establishment on Thursday evening, police said.
"It was a crime of the state," Carrillo said, alleging that Gonzalez had been killed because of USO's longstanding opposition to foreign oil companies operating in Colombia.

William Giraldo, a Bogota-based spokesman for the state oil company Ecopetrol, said he was unable to comment on the extent of the strike in Barrancabermeja because union demonstrators had formed a picket line outside the company's headquarters and were preventing all access to the building.
"I still don't have the company's official version," he said.
